observations: The run is complete, single-process evidence with matching run_start/run_end and intact deployment provenance.
The single Win32 menu-pointer owner still produced an uncontrollable pointer in-headset; the user had to return to the physical mouse.

The shipped analog controller-state transaction is now exercised and movement still reaches full magnitude, but walking remains unacceptable and the user reports jump height of only about two centimetres.

Horizontal-only visual-body compensation is exercised with zero vertical pelvis offset in all sampled room-scale writes, but physical room-scale displacement does not drive the walking animation expected from stick locomotion.
Arm safety now refuses many unsafe VR writes; this prevents some extreme takeover but visibly snaps the arms back to native animation as the Sense controllers move, so Body IK remains unusable.

Tracked handgrip-to-tip geometry strongly confirms local -Z as the Sense tip pointing axis, but shots still occur in visibly incorrect directions/origins. The remaining weapon failure is downstream of simple tip-axis selection.
The user requires shots to leave the visible weapon barrel. A temporary gameplay controller ray should be reintroduced only as a diagnostic alignment aid, not as production ballistics.
No playability gate advances from this run. Previously validated stereo, tracking, recenter and snap-turn contracts remain the stable baseline.
